item.title: IND v NZ 2026: “No one understood what he was,” Harbhajan sympathizes with Ishan Kishan after match-winning 76 in 2nd T20I
item.description: Ishan Kishan put on a show with the bat in India’s dominant seven-wicket victory over New Zealand in the second T20I at the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium, Raipur on Friday (January 23). Batting at No. 3, the southpaw slammed 76 off 32 balls with 11 fours and 4 sixes. item.title: IND v NZ 2026: “Showed why he is number one T20 batter,” Shivam Dube’s rich praise for Suryakumar Yadav after Raipur T20I
item.description: India’s T20I skipper Suryakumar Yadav endured a lean patch with the bat last year. He managed to score only 218 runs across 21 matches and 19 innings, averaging just over 13, with the best score of 47* to his credit. With only two weeks remaining for the T20 World Cup 2026, the Men in Blue are currently hosting New Zealand in a five-match T20I series. item.title: Bangladesh officially out of T20 World Cup 2026, ICC confirms Scotland as replacement
item.description: The International Cricket Council (ICC) on Saturday (January 24) confirmed that Scotland will replace Bangladesh at the Men’s T20 World Cup 2026, slated to be held in India and Sri Lanka from February 7 to March 8. Bangladesh lost their place in the 20-team tournament after refusing to travel to India, citing security reasons. item.title: WATCH: Mohsin Naqvi says Pakistan government will take final call on T20 World Cup participation after Bangladesh’s removal
item.description: Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chief Mohsin Naqvi on Saturday (January 24) said that Pakistan government will take a final call on national team’s participation in the upcoming T20 World Cup, following Bangladesh’s ouster from the marquee event. item.title: “Whatever the government says…,” Rajeev Shukla shares BCCI’s stance on India-Pakistan bilateral cricket
item.description: BCCI vice president Rajeev Shukla on Saturday (January 24) reiterated that India will not engage in a bilateral series with Pakistan without the approval of the Indian government. Shukla stressed that the cricket board will follow the government’s directives owing to the strained political relations between two nations.
